title: Seasonality-aware usage signal synthesis and guardrails for cost/latency monitoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem summary: The Console's usage/cost/latency alerts are generating noisy or missed signals during predictable seasonal patterns (e.g., daily/weekly batch jobs, end-of-month billing spikes, marketing campaigns). Current thresholds and single-model z-score style detectors do not account for seasonality and multivariate coupling between metrics (requests, tokens, GPU-hours, p50/p95 latency), causing frequent false positives and degraded trust in alerts.

Goal: Implement a seasonality-aware signal synthesis layer and a small ensemble of detectors that run in the usage analytics pipeline to reduce false positives without degrading sensitivity to real incidents. Provide per-customer and per-route baselines, automatic pattern detection (daily/weekly/quarterly), and an orchestration layer that escalates only when multiple orthogonal signals indicate anomalous behavior. Expose configuration and feedback in the Console for adjustments and triage notes.
acceptance_criteria: New signal synthesis stage ingests raw time-series (requests, tokens, cost, p50/p95 latency) and produces de-seasonalized baselines for hourly, daily, and weekly windows.
Detection ensemble (residual-AR, rolling-robust-z, and percentile-change) produces an anomaly score between 0-1 and a small explainability payload (dominant contributing metric and window).

Alerting pipeline only fires Pager/Slack/Console notifications when ensemble score > 0.85 and at least two metrics contribute >= 30% to the score, or when score > 0.98 for any single critical metric (cost, p95 latency).
Reduction in false-positive alert rate for high-volume customers by >= 45% in A/B test against current detector over a 2-week window.
Rollout plan completed: feature-gated by org-level toggle, can be rolled back in 5 minutes, and has a dedicated dashboard showing pre/post comparison and precision/recall estimation.
Runbook updated with triage steps, and a pager duty playbook for degradation-to-fallback scenarios.
implementation_steps: 1) Data contract: finalize schema for synthesized signals; add fields to analytics topic (de-seasonalized_baseline, seasonality_periods, ensemble_score, explainability_tags).
2) Pipeline stage: implement Spark/Beam job (or Flink) to compute STL-style decomposition per customer-route, keeping lightweight defaults for low-cardinality orgs.
3) Detectors: implement three compact detectors in Rust/Go microservice: residual-AR(1) model, rolling-median robust z-score, and percentile-delta with changepoint smoothing.
4) Scoring/orchestration: build orchestrator that normalizes per-metric signal, computes weighted ensemble score, applies hysteresis and dampening for short-lived spikes.
5) Alerting integration: hook into existing console alerting backend; add new alert templates and subscriptions; support opt-in per-org testing mode.
6) Observability: publish debug metrics and histograms (false_positive_rate_est, detection_latency_ms, ensemble_latency_ms) and a dashboard for the rollout cohort.
7) QA and A/B: create synthetic workloads (steady, seasonal, sudden spike, multi-metric correlated) and run end-to-end A/B test with ~80 orgs across tiers.
8) Rollout and rollback controls: add org toggle, migration job for historical context, and a quick rollback route in the console.
data_schema: Raw inputs: timestamp (ISO8601), org_id, route_id, request_count, token_count, gpu_seconds, cost_usd, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms
Synthesized outputs: de_seasonalized_value, baseline_value, seasonality_periods (list of strings), ensemble_score (float 0-1), explainability_tags (list)
Retention: keep 90 days of synthesized signals; cold storage for full raw timeseries at 13 months.
alerting_policy: Primary: ensemble_score >= 0.85 AND at least two metrics flagged with contribution >= 30% triggers Alert-Group1 (Console + Slack).
High-severity: ensemble_score >= 0.98 for metrics cost_usd or p95_latency_ms triggers PagerDuty escalation immediately.
Suppression: automatic mute for short-lived (<= 10 minutes) deviations and configurable silence windows (org-level).
Adaptive thresholds: for low-volume orgs (request_count < 1000/day) use longer smoothing window and reduce sensitivity.
runbook_excerpt: Step 1: Validate alert details in Console; check explainability_tags to see top contributing metric and window.
Step 2: Confirm seasonality context via the synthesized baseline panel; if deviation aligns with known campaign or billing period, mark as maintenance and close.
Step 3: If multiple independent metrics spike and p95_latency > target, run tail-sampling and trace lookups. Escalate to infra on-call if increase persists >30 minutes.
Step 4: In case of false positives discovered, annotate org toggle and submit 'alert tuning' note to Alerts backlog (ENG-XXXX).
testing_plan: Unit tests for decomposition and detectors with deterministic seeds.
Integration tests in staging with replayed historical customer bursts (including end-of-month billing and weekly jobs).
A/B experiment: 2-week live test comparing new ensemble vs legacy detector; measure precision/recall and MTTA/MTTR.
Chaos test: inject noisy spikes and system clock shifts to validate stability and hysteresis.
observability_checks: Latency: end-to-end detection pipeline <= 8s 99th percentile for hourly aggregations.
Accuracy: provide per-org precision/recall estimate in dashboard; aim for precision >= 0.75 in initial rollout.
Resource: CPU/RAM profiles for the microservice and additional load on streaming job; ensure <15% infra overhead on peak.
